     health benefits including improved heart health and better
     energy levels. Bananas come in their natural packaging with
     a peel that turns from green to yellow as they ripen, and
     they can be eaten fresh, added to smoothies, or used in
     baking.
  3. Cherry
     Cherries are small, round fruits that come in shades of
     red, dark red, and black, each variety offering its own
     unique taste profile from sweet to slightly tart. These
     delicious fruits are packed with antioxidants and have been
     enjoyed for centuries in both sweet and savory dishes
     across many cultures worldwide. Cherries have a short
     season, making them a special treat when they are available
     at farmers markets and grocery stores during summer
     months.
  4. Date
     Dates are sweet, chewy fruits that come from date palm
     trees and have been a dietary staple in Middle Eastern and
     North African regions for thousands of years. They are
     naturally high in sugar, fiber, and various minerals like
     magnesium and potassium, making them an excellent energy
     source for both athletes and those needing a quick
     pick-me-up snack. Dates can be eaten fresh or dried, used
     in baking, stuffed with nuts or cheese, or ground into a
     paste for various culinary applications.
